entities.summary: Htilominlo, also called Nadaungmya(နားတောင်းများ, or Zeya Theinkha Uzana, was king of the Pagan dynasty of Burma from 1211 to 1235. His 24-year reign marked the beginning of the gradual decline of Pagan dynasty. It was the first to see the impact of over a century of continuous growth of tax-free religious wealth, which had greatly reduced the potential tax base. Htilominlo was the last of the temple builders although most of his temples were in remote lands outside the Pagan region, reflecting the deteriorating state of royal treasury.
